text: What single capability does a loop add to the model?
choices: The ability to call the same code twice
The program counter can move backwards, so running time is no longer bounded by program length
The ability to store more than one value
explanation: Without a backward jump, a program executes each line at most once and its running time is bounded by its length. Once the counter can go back, a three-line loop can run for a billion steps or forever — which is what makes loops powerful and dangerous, and it is exactly the step from the parity machine to Turing's.
